The season that comes after autumn is winter.

The author employs a third-person omniscient point of view, observing the detective’s narration from an external perspective while commenting on the audience's reaction ("one could not help but admire"). The narrative style is analytical and descriptive, focusing on the qualities of the detective's speech rather than dramatizing the events themselves. The tone of the passage is objective and appreciative, mirroring the "clinical detachment" it describes in the detective. It maintains a formal, critical distance, evaluating the narrative technique with precision and restraint.
